record.paper_title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Directional Hessian convergence along a ray
record.original_question: Let f: R^n -> R be convex, let x(t) = (t, 0, ..., 0), and assume in addition that the Hessian Hf(x(t)) exists for all t > 0. Can the one-sided limit lim_{t↓0} Hf(x(t)) fail to exist? The paper explicitly treats this as an open second-order analogue of the directional gradient question, and also notes analogous infinite-dimensional and higher-order variants.

evidence.quote: F. Giannessi asked also several “second-order” questions. Namely, assuming additionally that Hessian Hf (x(t)) exists for all t > 0, where Hf (x(t)) stands for the Hessian of f at x(t), he asked whether: the limit lim t↓0 Hf (x(t)); (2)
might not exist. Infinite dimensional as well as higher order and other cases of this question can be considered.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be a convex function, and consider the ray $x(t)=(t,0,\dots,0)$ for $t>0$. Assume that the Hessian $Hf(x(t))$ (the matrix of second-order partial derivatives of $f$) exists for every $t>0$. Determine whether it is possible that the one-sided limit
$$\lim_{t\downarrow 0} Hf(x(t))$$
fails to exist (in the space of symmetric $n\times n$ matrices). Equivalently, must this limit always exist under the stated hypotheses? Analogous formulations may be considered in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces and for higher-order derivatives.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to F. Giannessi as a second-order analogue of the directional gradient problem for convex functions, is recorded as an open problem in surveys of directional convergence of subgradients/Hessians of convex functions. No resolution was found in the search results.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Convergence of Subgradients of Convex Functions Along Directions: Perspectives and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on the directional convergence of subgradients, subdifferentials and Hessians of convex functions are recalled and posed.
status_evidence.claim: The second-order Hessian directional limit question is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Limiting behaviour of the approximate first order and second order directional derivatives for a convex function
status_evidence.snippet: Limiting behaviour of approximate first- and second-order directional derivatives for convex functions.
status_evidence.claim: Related second-order directional limit questions remain studied without a general resolution of Giannessi's Hessian question.
